Rev 01 - Full-Scope Update / Draft for Review
HVAC, Electrical, Decorative Finishes, Painting, Plaster and Tiling

blocks.text: Basis of Report

• The Arabic preventive-maintenance sheets supplied for central chillers, chilled-water pumps, AHU/FCU equipment and DX systems were converted into auditable task libraries with frequencies, acceptance controls and required evidence.
• The supplied FM classification was incorporated as one Hard FM, Soft FM and Strategic FM service model.

• Electrical, decorative finishes, painting, plaster and tiling are now developed to the same control depth as HVAC, including preventive tasks, repair methods, quality hold points and escalation rules.

• Final frequencies and limits must be validated against the actual asset register, OEM manuals, drawings, warranties, authority requirements, operating duty and contract. The most stringent applicable requirement prevails.

Important use limitation
This report is a premium technical framework for tendering, mobilization and operations. It does not replace project-specific design documents, statutory certification, OEM instructions, approved method statements, risk assessments, permits to work or specialist engineering decisions.
Approval and Authorization
A structured route from governance and mobilization to trade-level task libraries and reporting.

Reading priority
Sections 03-09 define the operating model; Sections 10-15 contain the detailed trade standards; Sections 16-21 define response performance, resources, risk, governance and sample records.
A premium, evidence-led operating model for reliable systems and consistently high-quality finishes.
EXECUTIVE INTENT  Purpose and Outcome

This report establishes one technical standard for operating and maintaining HVAC, electrical systems and premium architectural finishes. Basic checklist actions are converted into controlled work packages with clear frequencies, competent-person requirements, acceptance criteria, evidence, escalation and lifecycle feedback.

The model is suitable for high-profile residential, hospitality, commercial and mixed-use assets where equipment reliability and visual presentation carry equal importance. Technical rooms, public areas, resident and guest routes, and signature spaces are managed through different inspection intensities, while all defects are controlled through one CAFM, quality and governance process.
Six detailed technical disciplines governed through one integrated maintenance framework.
Expected Operational Benefits

columns:
Reliability
Reduced unplanned failure through risk-based PPM, baseline readings and condition trending.

Safety and compliance
Controlled permits, isolation, inspection, testing and auditable certification.
rows:
Premium appearance
Rapid detection and consistent restoration using approved samples, finish codes and batch control.

Lifecycle and transparency
Readings, photographs, costs and condition grades are converted into auditable renewal and CAPEX decisions.

blocks.text: Critical Success Conditions
• A verified asset register with location, criticality, make/model/serial, warranty and maintainable components.
• Approved finishes schedule, colour/texture sample library and adequate attic stock for visible materials.
• Competent authorized supervisors and technicians with calibrated tools and clear permit responsibilities.
• CAFM work orders that capture labour, materials, readings, photographs, failure code, downtime, cause and verification.
• Client approval of property-specific response targets, access rules, service windows, shutdowns and aesthetic standards.
Hard FM, Soft FM and Strategic FM aligned to one client experience and asset-value objective.
Operating Principle

Hard FM delivers technical reliability and safe asset operation. Soft FM protects the occupant experience and provides immediate visibility of defects. Strategic FM converts operational data into energy, risk, vendor, renewal and lifecycle decisions. The three service types therefore share one helpdesk, inspection regime, escalation process, reporting calendar and client governance forum.
Cross-Service Interfaces

columns:
Cleaning
Report stains, leaks, loose finishes, failed lighting and recurring dirt patterns; use finish-compatible chemicals.

Security / reception
Raise public-area defects immediately, control access and support barriers and communication.
rows:
BMS / helpdesk
Convert alarms, complaints and trends into prioritized work orders and verify closure.

Fire and life safety
Coordinate impairments, emergency lighting, fire stopping, smoke control and shutdown permits.

Projects / fit-out
Control handover documents, warranties, finish samples and as-built changes.

Procurement / stores
Maintain approved spares and finish materials with batch, shelf-life and shade records.

blocks.text: Interfaces and Specialist Boundaries

• Plumbing/drainage, waterproofing, façade, structural, fire alarm, fire-fighting, lifts, access control and ELV may be separate specialist scopes. The originating defect must be corrected before finish reinstatement.

• Structural or active cracking, hazardous materials, high-voltage or exceptional live work, major refrigerant intervention, façade rope access and statutory fire/life-safety certification require authorized specialists.
• Major replacement, redesign and capital improvement are controlled through variation/CAPEX, not disguised as routine PPM.
Service Zoning for Premium Assets

rows: Main lobbies, reception, show units, VIP routes, branded areas
Daily visual inspection; hazards immediate; visible cosmetic restoration prioritized within the premium-service window.
Lift lobbies, corridors, amenities and public interfaces
Daily/weekly inspection based on traffic; safety, visibility and user impact drive priority.
Stores, service corridors, staff areas, loading and car parks
Weekly/monthly inspection; safety and functionality first, with planned cosmetic repair.
Plant rooms, electrical rooms, roofs and service shafts
Risk- and asset-based PPM with controlled access, housekeeping and statutory safety.

blocks.text: Risk-based planning, controlled execution and continuous improvement.
Maintenance Mix

Work triggered by readings, wear, finish condition, pressure drop, thermal image, vibration or defect grade.
Trend analysis to identify deterioration before service failure or visible damage.
Controlled response to alarms, complaints, failures and safety defects.
Replacement or refurbishment based on condition, obsolescence, risk, cost and business impact.

blocks.text: Proposed Work Priority and SLA Matrix

rows: Life safety, exposed live part, critical outage, falling finish, major leak
Attend <= 15 min; make safe immediately; continuous action and executive escalation.
Major service degradation, high-visibility defect, partial outage, active water damage, repeated trip
Attend <= 30 min; stabilize <= 2 h; permanent repair plan same shift.
Localized functional defect with acceptable temporary condition
Attend <= 4 h; close normally within 24-48 h or approved parts lead time.
Non-critical improvement, planned touch-up, minor BOH aesthetic defect
Plan within 1 business day; close within agreed maintenance window, normally 5-10 days.

The response and restoration times above are proposed premium baselines. Final commitments must be approved against property occupancy, staffing, access, contract, spare availability and specialist dependencies.

blocks.text: BMS and Condition Data Use
• Critical alarms are linked to the correct asset, location, response team and escalation tree.
• Overrides, disabled points, unstable control loops, temperature excursions and repeated trips are managed as exceptions, not permanent workarounds.

• Baseline trends are retained for chiller performance, chilled-water delta-T, pump current/pressure, AHU temperature/valve position, generator/UPS condition, electrical demand/power factor and environmental conditions affecting finishes.
• Finish photographs and records are searchable by zone, surface, finish code and defect type.

blocks.text: Detailed preventive, condition-based and corrective controls derived from the supplied HVAC checklists.
Objectives and Acceptance Philosophy

HVAC maintenance shall maintain thermal comfort, indoor-air quality, plant safety, energy performance and equipment life. The task library expands the supplied chiller, chilled-water pump, AHU/FCU and DX maintenance sheets into measurable controls. Readings are compared with design/OEM requirements and the equipment’s own clean, stable baseline rather than treated as isolated numbers.

columns:
No hidden bypass
Safeties, flow proof, alarms and interlocks are tested and never left bypassed.

Readings before opinion
Temperature, pressure, current, vibration, flow and trend data support diagnosis.
rows:
Clean heat transfer
Filters, coils, tubes, strainers and airflow paths are maintained to prevent avoidable loss.

Dry and hygienic air side
Drain pans, traps, condensate lines and internal surfaces remain clean and free-draining.

Stable control
Sensors, valves, dampers and BMS logic respond without hunting or permanent overrides.

Root-cause closure
Trips, low delta-T, leaks and condensate problems trigger analysis, not repeated resets.

HVAC escalation triggers
Repeated safety trip, refrigerant leak, compressor abnormality, significant performance deterioration, persistent low chilled-water delta-T, biological contamination, uncontrolled condensation or any condition outside OEM safe operating limits requires engineering escalation and an approved recovery plan.
Power continuity, safe isolation, protection integrity and auditable testing for all LV systems.
Objectives and Acceptance Philosophy

Electrical maintenance shall protect life, prevent fire and equipment damage, maintain power continuity and preserve the integrity of protection, earthing and distribution systems. Only competent authorized personnel may perform electrical work. De-energized work is the default; exceptional live diagnostic activity must be formally justified, risk assessed and approved.

columns:
Protection first
Breaker, relay, RCD, earth-fault and interlock settings remain controlled and tested.

Thermal condition
Thermography is performed under meaningful load and defects are confirmed by inspection.
rows:
Verified isolation
LOTO, test-before-touch and controlled re-energization are independently verified.

Continuity of supply
Generators, ATS, UPS and batteries are functionally tested with documented capacity.

Accurate records
Labels, schedules, settings, single-line diagrams and test certificates remain current.

Controlled rooms
Electrical rooms remain dry, secure, ventilated, clean and unobstructed.

Electrical escalation triggers
Arcing evidence, protection operation, unexplained hot spot, damaged insulation, exposed live part, recurrent trip, earth fault, transformer/generator abnormality or any failed protection/statutory test requires immediate risk control and authorized engineering review.
Premium appearance, secure fixings and consistent material matching across visible architectural features.
Definition and Control Intent

Decorative finishes include architectural wall and ceiling features, cladding, panels, mouldings, joinery, veneers, laminates, metal and glass features, mirrors, trims, signage, artwork interfaces and sealants. Each critical visible finish is treated as an asset: coded, photographed, inspected, maintained and linked to an approved sample and cleaning method.
Premium Visual Acceptance Standard
• No loose, sharp, unstable or falling component; safety defects are isolated immediately.
• Alignment, joints, grain/pattern, sheen, trims and interfaces remain consistent with the approved installation.
• Repairs use approved compatible materials with traceable finish code and batch; substitutions require approval.
• Moisture, movement, impact or cleaning damage is corrected before cosmetic reinstatement.
• Acceptance is checked under actual lighting and normal viewing conditions.

blocks.text: Controlled surface preparation, colour matching, coating compatibility and premium visual finish.
Definition and Control Intent

Painting maintenance covers internal and external decorative coatings, metal protective coatings, timber paint systems, wet-area finishes and operational markings. Touch-up is not simply applying paint: the defect source, substrate, primer, product, code, sheen, batch, environment and final appearance are controlled.
Defect Diagnosis Before Painting

rows: Investigate moisture, heat, incompatible coating or trapped contamination; do not overpaint active blistering.
Determine adhesion failure, weak substrate, poor preparation or moisture; remove to sound edge.
Separate coating crack from moving plaster or structural crack; repair the source first.
Identify salts and water path; clean and dry substrate and use a compatible system.
Correct moisture/ventilation cause and use an approved cleaning and coating system.
Prepare metal to sound condition and reinstate compatible corrosion protection.
Use approved sample and repaint a logical plane where local touch-up remains visible.

blocks.text: Sound substrates, crack diagnosis, controlled repairs and accurate finish restoration.
Definition and Control Intent

Plaster maintenance covers gypsum and cementitious wall/ceiling finishes, corners, beads and repair interfaces. Correct diagnosis is essential: active or structural cracking and moisture-related failure are not concealed by filler and paint. Loose overhead plaster is treated as an immediate safety risk.
Crack and Defect Classification

rows: Fine stable surface crack with no displacement or recurrence; compatible cosmetic repair may be suitable after confirmation.

Loss of bond shown by bulging, movement or sounding; map and remove unsafe loose material.
Widening, displacement, diagonal pattern or repeated opening; make safe and refer to structural engineer.

blocks.text: Safe, bonded, aligned and watertight floor and wall finishes with controlled material matching.
Definition and Control Intent

Tiling maintenance covers ceramic, porcelain and natural-stone floor and wall tiles, skirtings, trims, grout, sealants and movement joints. Safety is first, followed by water integrity, bond, alignment and visual matching. Wet-area repairs must protect waterproofing, drainage falls and movement joints.
Immediate Safety Conditions
• Cracked or chipped tile with sharp edge, loose tile, raised tile, trip point or unstable wall tile is isolated and made safe immediately.
• Ponding, recurring wetness, failed sealant or leakage below a wet area triggers waterproofing/plumbing investigation before cosmetic repair.
• Designed movement joints are never filled with rigid grout, adhesive or plaster.
• Obsolete or shade-sensitive tiles require controlled stock and a client-approved matching strategy.
